unit: Unit 3: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Meaning of Business, Profession, and Method of Accounting
explain: Business includes any trade, commerce, manufacture, or single commercial venture with a profit motive.
Profession includes vocation and requires specialized learning or skilled knowledge.
Illegality of a business does not exempt its profits from being taxed under PGBP.
Taxpayers can follow either cash or mercantile system of accounting regularly employed.
Government subsidies and interest on enhanced compensation are taxed in the year of receipt under special rules.

flow.title: Taxability Determination of Business/Profession Income
steps: Identify activity type
Determine regular accounting system
Compute profits per accounting mode
Include special receipts on cash basis
Tax under head PGBP

topics.example: An architect earning professional fees records income under the mercantile system, but any government subsidy received is taxed in the year it actually arrives.
remember: 10 Income Computation and Disclosure Standards (ICDSs) apply to non-exempt mercantile taxpayers.
mistakes: Thinking illegal business profits are tax-free; income from illegal activities is fully taxable.

quiz.q: Which head of income taxes income from an illegal betting business?
o: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
quiz.why: The illegality of a business does not exempt its income from being taxed under PGBP.

quiz.q: Under section 278, when is government subsidy deemed to be taxable income?
quiz.why: Section 278 specifically mandates taxing assistance like subsidies in the tax year of actual receipt.

topics.title: Incomes Chargeable Under PGBP
explain: Profits from any business or profession carried on at any time during the tax year are taxable under PGBP.
Compensation for termination or modification of management contracts or agencies is business income.
Export incentives such as profit on sale of import licenses, cash assistance, and duty drawbacks are taxable.
Value of any benefit or perquisite arising from business or profession is chargeable.
Partner's salary, bonus, interest, or commission received from a firm is treated as business income.

flow.title: Charging Test under Section 26
steps: Check if activity is business/profession
Identify specific receipts or benefits
Verify if covered under section 26
Exclude exempt share of partner profit
Tax residual sum under PGBP

topics.example: A company providing rent-free accommodation to its legal advisor in return for services generates taxable business perquisite income for the lawyer.
remember: Partner's share of profits in a firm's total income is exempt from tax in the partner's hands.
mistakes: Taxing residential letting income under PGBP when an assessee carries on letting business; it goes to Income from House Property.

quiz.q: Income from letting out residential houses by a person in such business is taxable under:
o: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
quiz.why: Income from letting out residential houses is specifically excepted from PGBP and taxed under Income from House Property.

quiz.q: Salary received by a partner from their firm is taxable in partner's hands under which head?
o: Profits and Gains of Business or Profession
quiz.why: Partner remuneration is specifically treated as business income under section 26(vii).

topics.title: Speculation Business and Speculative Transactions
explain: A speculation business is treated as distinct and separate from any other business carried on by the assessee.
Speculative transaction means settling a contract without actual delivery of commodities, stocks, or shares.
Hedging contracts for raw materials, stocks, forward contracts, and screen-based derivative trades are non-speculative.
Speculation losses can only be set off against profits of another speculation business.
Companies buying and selling shares are deemed speculative unless their main income is HP, CG, IFOS, or banking.

flow.title: Classification of Speculative Transaction
steps: Examine contract settlement method
Check if settled without physical delivery
Verify specific non-speculative exceptions
Classify as speculative or non-speculative
Apply isolated loss set-off rules

topics.example: Entering a raw cotton forward contract to protect a cotton mill against price rise is non-speculative hedging.
remember: Speculation loss can be set off ONLY against speculation profits, not normal business profits.
mistakes: Assuming screen-based derivative trading in recognized stock exchanges is speculative; it is legally non-speculative.

quiz.q: Which of the following is considered a non-speculative transaction?
o: Buying and selling shares without physical delivery
Settling gold contracts by price difference only
Hedging contract by a raw material user against price rise
Trading in unlisted options off-market without delivery
quiz.why: Hedging contracts to guard against raw material price fluctuations are explicitly excluded from speculative transactions.

quiz.q: Losses arising from a speculation business can be set off against:
quiz.why: Section 113 mandates that speculation losses can only be set off against speculation profits.

topics.title: Rent, Rates, Taxes, Repairs and Insurance for Assets
explain: Deduction is allowed for rent paid by a tenant for premises occupied for business or profession.
Current repairs to premises, machinery, plant, and furniture used for business are fully deductible.
Capital expenditure incurred on repairs or replacements is strictly disallowed as a revenue deduction.
Land revenue, local rates, municipal taxes, and insurance premia paid for business assets are allowed.
If assets are used partly for non-business purposes, only a fair proportionate expense is allowed.

flow.title: Deductibility of Repair and Maintenance Expenses
steps: Check asset usage for business
Identify nature of repair expenditure
Separate revenue from capital repairs
Apportion if used partly for personal use
Deduct allowable proportionate revenue sum

topics.example: If an entrepreneur uses 60% of a building for their office and 40% for residence, 60% of municipal taxes and current repairs are allowed as PGBP deduction.
remember: Capital repairs cannot be deducted as revenue expenses but increase asset block for depreciation.
mistakes: Claiming cost of total replacement or reconstruction as current repairs under section 28.

quiz.q: What type of repairs to machinery is allowable as a deduction under section 28?
o: Arrears of repairs for past 5 years
quiz.why: Only current repairs of a revenue nature are deductible under section 28.

quiz.q: If a tenant incurs capital expenditure on renovating a leased office building, how is it treated?
o: Disallowed completely without any tax benefit
Deducted under section 34 as general loss
quiz.why: Under section 33(6), capital expenditure on leased buildings is treated as a deemed building owned by the assessee for depreciation.

topics.title: Deductions for Employee Welfare Funds and Schemes
explain: Employer contribution to recognized provident fund or approved superannuation fund is allowed.
Employer contribution to an approved pension scheme u/s 124 is restricted to 14% of employee's salary.
Salary for pension scheme calculation includes basic salary and dearness allowance forming part of pay.
Employer contribution to an approved gratuity fund under an irrevocable trust is deductible.
Employee contributions collected by employer must be deposited in the fund on or before the return filing due date u/s 263(1).

flow.title: Employee Contribution Deposit Rule
steps: Receive employee contribution to PF/ESI
Treat sum as income u/s 2(49)(o)
Deposit sum into welfare fund
Check deposit date against return due date
Allow deduction if paid on/before due date

topics.example: Employer collects ₹10,000 PF from employees. If deposited on or before the due date of return filing, it is deducted from income, leaving net effect zero.
remember: Max deduction for employer pension contribution u/s 124 is 14% of (Basic Salary + DA forming part).
mistakes: Depositing employee PF contributions after the return due date and still expecting a deduction.

quiz.q: An employer contributes to a pension scheme u/s 124. What is the maximum allowable deduction percentage of salary?
quiz.why: Section 29(1)(b) restricts allowable employer pension contribution to 14% of employee salary.

quiz.q: Employee's PF contribution collected by an employer is deductible in employer's hands only if deposited on or before:
o: Due date specified u/s 263(1) for filing return
quiz.why: Under section 29(1)(e), employee welfare contributions are deductible only if credited to employee account on or before the return due date.

topics.title: Insurance Premia and Bad Debts Deductions
explain: Insurance premium paid on business stock or stores is fully deductible under section 30(a).
Health insurance premium paid by an employer for employees by non-cash mode is deductible u/s 30(c).
Bad debt is allowed as a deduction u/s 31(2) if it is written off as irrecoverable in the books.
The debt must have been included in income computation of the current or an earlier tax year.
Subsequent recovery of a previously allowed bad debt is taxed as business income in the year of recovery u/s 38(1)(d).

flow.title: Bad Debt Deduction and Recovery Flow
steps: Offer debt as income in current/earlier year
Write off debt in books as irrecoverable
Claim PGBP deduction u/s 31(2)
Recover debt sum in subsequent year
Tax recovery excess as deemed profit u/s 38(1)(d)

topics.example: A merchant writes off ₹50,000 bad debt in books. Next year, ₹30,000 is recovered from the debtor; this ₹30,000 becomes deemed business profit in the recovery year.
remember: Mere provision for bad and doubtful debts is NOT deductible; actual write-off in accounts is required.
mistakes: Paying employee health insurance premium in cash and claiming deduction under section 30.

quiz.q: Employer pays health insurance premium for employees. To be deductible u/s 30(c), payment must be made:
o: Through any mode other than cash
quiz.why: Section 30(c) explicitly requires health insurance premium to be paid by any mode other than cash.

quiz.q: An AO allowed ₹80,000 bad debt out of ₹1,20,000 claimed in T.Y. 2025-26. In T.Y. 2026-27, ₹1,00,000 is recovered. Taxable amount u/s 38(1)(d) is:
quiz.why: Unallowed debt was ₹40,000 (120k-80k). Recovery of ₹1,00,000 exceeds unallowed part by ₹60,000 (100k - 40k).

topics.title: Specific Business Deductions - Interest, Bonus, ZCB & Family Planning
explain: Bonus and commission paid to employees are deductible if not payable as profit/dividend.
Interest on borrowed capital for business is deductible; however, interest during asset acquisition phase must be capitalised.
Discount on Zero Coupon Bonds (ZCB) is deductible on a pro-rata basis over the bond's life.
Revenue family planning expenses are deductible for corporate assessees; capital family planning expenses are allowed in 5 equal annual installments.
Securities Transaction Tax (STT) and Commodity Transaction Tax (CTT) paid are deductible if income is taxed under PGBP.

flow.title: Treatment of Borrowing Interest for Asset Purchase
steps: Borrow capital for capital asset purchase
Track period from borrowing to first put to use
Capitalise interest for pre-use period into cost
Track period post first put to use
Claim post-use interest as PGBP deduction

topics.example: A company borrows funds on July 1 to buy machinery. Machinery is put to use on Jan 1. July to Dec interest is added to asset cost; Jan onwards interest is revenue deduction.
remember: Capital expenditure on family planning is allowable ONLY to companies, spread over 5 years.
mistakes: Claiming family planning capital expenditure deduction for non-corporate assessees like sole proprietorships or firms.

quiz.q: S Ltd. borrowed capital on 1st July 2026 for machinery put to use on 1st January 2027. Interest from July to December 2026 shall be:
quiz.why: Interest from borrowing date till the date asset is first put to use must be capitalised.

quiz.q: Capital expenditure on promoting family planning amongst employees is allowable as deduction to:
quiz.why: Section 32(i) restricts family planning expenditure deductions strictly to corporate assessees.

topics.title: Normal Depreciation and Block of Assets
explain: Depreciation deduction under section 33 is mandatory, regardless of whether claimed in return.
Assets must be owned (wholly/partly) and used for business/profession during the tax year.
Depreciation is calculated on the Written Down Value (WDV) of a 'Block of Assets'.
Block of assets means a group of assets falling in same class having same depreciation rate.
If an asset acquired during the year is put to use for less than 180 days, depreciation is restricted to 50% of prescribed rate.

flow.title: Depreciation Allowance Calculation
steps: Group assets into blocks by rate and class
Determine WDV at end of tax year
Separate assets put to use < 180 days
Apply 50% rate to < 180 days assets
Apply 100% rate to balance block WDV

topics.example: A computer (40% rate) bought on Jan 2 and put to use on Jan 5 (less than 180 days) receives 20% depreciation in the year of acquisition.
remember: Computers and computer software fall under 40% depreciation block; general plant & machinery under 15%.
mistakes: Applying the 50% depreciation restriction in subsequent years; it applies ONLY in the year of acquisition.

quiz.q: A firm acquired machinery during T.Y. 2026-27 but did not put it to use till 31.3.2027. Depreciation for T.Y. 2026-27 is:
quiz.why: Actual put-to-use in the tax year is an essential condition for claiming depreciation.

quiz.q: What is the prescribed normal rate of depreciation for general Plant & Machinery?
quiz.why: General plant & machinery falls under Block 18 with a 15% prescribed rate.

topics.title: Additional Depreciation and Power Undertakings Rules
explain: Additional depreciation @20% is allowed on new plant & machinery acquired by manufacturing or power sector units.
If put to use for less than 180 days in acquisition year, 10% is allowed in year 1 and remaining 10% in year 2.
Additional depreciation is NOT allowed on office appliances, road vehicles, second-hand machinery, or office-installed assets.
Power undertakings have the option to claim depreciation on Straight Line Method (SLM) on actual cost u/s 33(2).
When an SLM power asset is sold, deficiency is allowed as Terminal Depreciation u/s 33(10); excess WDV up to cost is taxed as Balancing Charge u/s 38(1)(b).

flow.title: Additional Depreciation Eligibility Test
steps: Check if assessee manufactures or generates power
Ensure taxpayer opted out of default tax regime u/s 202(4)
Verify asset is NEW plant & machinery
Ensure asset is NOT vehicle, office appliance, or office-installed
Grant 20% (or 10%+10% if <180 days) additional depreciation

topics.example: A factory buys new manufacturing machinery for ₹10 lakhs on Sept 1. Additional depreciation @20% (₹2 lakhs) is granted over and above normal 15% depreciation.
remember: Additional depreciation is available ONLY under the optional tax regime u/s 202(4), not default regime.
mistakes: Claiming additional depreciation on second-hand imported machinery or computers installed in office premises.

quiz.q: Additional depreciation under section 33(8) is NOT allowable on which of the following assets?
quiz.why: Section 33(8) explicitly excludes office appliances and road transport vehicles from additional depreciation.

quiz.q: A power concern sold an SLM asset (Cost ₹20L, WDV ₹12L) for ₹18L. What is the taxable Balancing Charge u/s 38(1)(b)?
quiz.why: Balancing charge is Sale Price minus WDV (18L - 12L = 6L), capped at total depreciation allowed.

topics.title: Determination of Actual Cost and WDV
explain: Actual cost means original acquisition cost to assessee minus subsidies, grants, and input tax credits (GST).
Individual cash payments exceeding ₹10,000 in a day for asset acquisition are excluded from actual cost.
Assets acquired via gift/inheritance take actual cost as WDV in hands of previous owner.
Personal building brought into business uses actual cost reduced by notional depreciation from acquisition date.
Closing WDV equals Opening WDV plus additions minus sales consideration received during the year.

flow.title: WDV Calculation for Block of Assets
steps: Start with Opening WDV of block
Add actual cost of new assets acquired
Deduct money payable/sale price for sold assets
Arrive at Net WDV at end of year
Calculate depreciation on Net WDV

topics.example: Dr. Soman bought a car for personal use at ₹5,25,000 and later brought it into practice when FMV was ₹2,50,000. Actual cost for depreciation remains ₹5,25,000.
remember: Notional depreciation adjustment for personal assets brought into business applies ONLY to buildings, not cars.
mistakes: Including cash payments above ₹10,000 made in a single day into the actual cost of an asset.

quiz.q: Personal car bought for ₹5,00,000 is brought into professional use when FMV is ₹3,00,000. Actual cost for PGBP depreciation is:
quiz.why: For assets other than buildings, actual cost to assessee is original purchase price, ignoring FMV change.

quiz.q: If an asset is acquired by paying ₹25,000 cash in a single day, how much is added to actual cost u/s 39?
quiz.why: Payments exceeding ₹10,000 in cash per day are completely excluded from actual cost under section 39.

topics.title: Carry Forward and Set-off of Unabsorbed Depreciation
explain: If current business profit is insufficient to absorb full depreciation, the unabsorbed portion becomes unabsorbed depreciation.
Unabsorbed depreciation can be set off against any head of income except 'Salaries'.
There is no time limit for carry forward of unabsorbed depreciation; it can be carried forward indefinitely.
Set-off is allowed even if the original business to which depreciation belonged has been discontinued.
Order of set-off: Current Year Depreciation FIRST, then Brought Forward Business Loss, then Unabsorbed Depreciation.

flow.title: Priority Order of Set-Off in Business Computation
steps: Compute Gross Business Income
Deduct Current Year Depreciation first
Deduct Brought Forward Business Loss second
Deduct Unabsorbed Depreciation third
Arrive at Net Taxable PGBP Income

topics.example: Mr. X has business income before depreciation of ₹16L and depreciation of ₹20L. ₹16L is absorbed, leaving ₹4L unabsorbed depreciation to carry forward indefinitely.
remember: Unabsorbed depreciation can be carried forward INDEFINITELY with no 8-year limit.
mistakes: Setting off brought forward business loss before deducting current year depreciation.

quiz.q: What is the time limit for carry forward of unabsorbed depreciation under section 33(11)?
quiz.why: Unabsorbed depreciation has no time limit and can be carried forward indefinitely until fully set off.

quiz.q: Unabsorbed depreciation CANNOT be set off against which head of income?
quiz.why: Section 33(11) allows set off of unabsorbed depreciation against any head of income except Salaries.

topics.title: Amortisation of Preliminary and VRS Expenditure
explain: Preliminary expenses incurred by resident non-corporate assessees or Indian companies are amortised over 5 years (1/5th each year).
Eligible preliminary expenses include project reports, market surveys, legal drafting, and registration fees.
Max preliminary expense limit: 5% of cost of project (or 5% of capital employed for Indian companies, whichever is higher).
Expenditure on Voluntary Retirement Scheme (VRS) under section 52 is amortised in 5 equal annual installments.
VRS deduction starts from the tax year in which the sum is actually paid.

flow.title: Preliminary Expenditure Amortisation Steps
steps: Sum up qualifying preliminary expenses
Calculate 5% of project cost / capital employed
Cap eligible expenses at maximum limit
Divide capped sum by 5 years
Claim 1/5th deduction per tax year

topics.example: XYZ Ltd. pays ₹25 lakhs to employees under a voluntary retirement scheme. It claims ₹5 lakhs (1/5th) as deduction each year for 5 consecutive years.
remember: Qualifying preliminary expense limit for non-corporate assessees is strictly 5% of Cost of Project.
mistakes: Claiming entire VRS expenditure in the single year of payment instead of spreading it over 5 years.

quiz.q: XYZ Ltd. paid ₹25 lakh for VRS during T.Y. 2026-27. What is the allowable deduction for T.Y. 2026-27 u/s 52?
quiz.why: Section 52 allows VRS expenditure deduction in 5 equal annual installments (25L / 5 = 5L).

quiz.q: What is the maximum limit of qualifying preliminary expenses for a resident individual?
quiz.why: For resident non-corporate taxpayers, the limit is strictly 5% of the Cost of Project.

topics.title: Expenditure on Scientific Research
explain: 100% of revenue and capital expenditure (excluding land cost) on in-house scientific research related to business is deductible.
In-house research expenses incurred within 3 years prior to business commencement (salaries & materials) are allowed in commencement year.
Contributions to outside approved research associations, universities, IITs, or national labs are 100% deductible.
Under default tax regime u/s 202(1), in-house research expenses are allowed, but contributions to outsiders are DISALLOWED.
No depreciation is allowed on any capital asset whose full cost was claimed as deduction under section 45.

flow.title: Scientific Research Deduction Analysis
steps: Identify if research is in-house or outside contribution
Exclude land cost from capital expenses
Check tax regime (default vs optional)
Allow in-house expenses in both regimes
Allow outside contributions ONLY under optional regime

topics.example: A pharma firm spends ₹3L revenue and ₹2.5L capital (excluding land) on in-house lab research. Entire ₹5.5L is deductible under both default and optional regimes.
remember: Outside contributions for scientific research are allowable ONLY if the taxpayer shifts out of default regime.
mistakes: Claiming 100% scientific research capital expenditure deduction on purchase of land.

quiz.q: Under the default tax regime u/s 202(1), which scientific research expenditure is allowable?
o: Contribution to IIT Delhi for research
In-house capital expenditure on machinery (excluding land)
Contribution to an approved Indian research company
Contribution to a university for social science research
quiz.why: In-house scientific research expenses are allowed under default tax regime, while outside contributions are disallowed.

quiz.q: Pre-commencement scientific research capital expenditure incurred within how many years prior to commencement is allowed?
quiz.why: Section 45 allows pre-commencement capital/revenue research expenses incurred within 3 years prior to commencement.

topics.title: Investment-Linked Tax Incentives for Specified Businesses
explain: 100% capital expenditure deduction is allowed for specified businesses like cold chains, warehousing for agricultural produce, hospitals (100+ beds), hotels (2-star+), etc.
Deduction excludes capital expenditure incurred on land, goodwill, and financial instruments.
Single-day cash payments exceeding ₹10,000 for asset purchase are excluded from specified business deduction.
Specified business assets must be used exclusively for specified business for a minimum period of 8 years.
This investment-linked deduction u/s 46 is available ONLY if the taxpayer shifts out of the default tax regime.

flow.title: Section 46 Deduction Test
steps: Verify specified business category
Ensure taxpayer opted out of default regime
Exclude costs of land, goodwill & financial instruments
Verify non-cash payment for sums > ₹10,000
Claim 100% capital expense deduction

topics.example: A company sets up a 100-bed hospital, spending ₹2 crore on building and ₹1.5 crore on land. ₹2 crore building cost is 100% deductible u/s 46; land cost is disallowed.
remember: If a specified asset is transferred to non-specified use within 8 years, total deduction minus notional depreciation is taxed as PGBP income.
mistakes: Claiming section 46 investment-linked deduction while paying tax under default tax regime u/s 202(1).

quiz.q: Which of the following capital expenditures is ELIGIBLE for deduction u/s 46?
o: Acquisition of land for cold chain facility
Purchase of goodwill for a new hotel
Construction of warehouse building for food grains
Purchase of financial shares for business
quiz.why: Section 46 specifically excludes land, goodwill, and financial instruments from capital expenditure deduction.

quiz.q: An asset claimed under section 46 must be used exclusively for specified business for how many years?
quiz.why: Section 46A(9)(a) mandates exclusive specified business usage for a period of 8 years.

topics.title: General Conditions for Allowable Deductions
explain: Section 34(1) is a residuary clause allowing revenue expenses expended wholly and exclusively for business/profession.
Expenditure must not be covered under sections 28 to 33, 44 to 46, and 52.
Expenditure must not be of capital nature or personal expenses of the assessee.
Expenses incurred for any purpose which is an offence or prohibited by law are strictly disallowed.
CSR expenditure u/s 135 of Companies Act and political party souvenir advertisements are explicitly disallowed.

flow.title: Residuary Test for Business Expenditure u/s 34
steps: Ensure not covered in specific sections 28-33/44-46
Confirm expense is revenue and non-personal
Verify incurred wholly for business
Check non-offence and non-CSR compliance
Allow full revenue deduction

topics.example: Freebies given to doctors by pharma companies violate medical regulations, making them expenses prohibited by law and disallowed u/s 34.
remember: Penalty paid for infringement of law is disallowed, but compensatory damages for contract delay are allowable.
mistakes: Treating Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) expenditure as an allowable business deduction.

quiz.q: Which of the following expenditures is ALLOWABLE as a deduction under section 34(1)?
o: Penalty paid for breach of statutory law
Compensatory damages paid for delay in contract execution
quiz.why: Compensatory damages are commercial in nature and allowable, unlike fines for breaking laws or CSR.

quiz.q: An essential condition for claiming deduction under section 34(1) is:
o: Expenditure must be capital in nature
Expenditure must be wholly & exclusively for business
Expenditure must create an enduring capital asset
Expenditure must be for personal use
quiz.why: Section 34(1) requires expenditure to be laid out wholly and exclusively for business/profession purposes.

topics.title: Disallowances for Income-tax and TDS Defaults
explain: Income-tax, surcharge, or cess paid is strictly disallowed as a PGBP deduction u/s 35(a).
Tax paid by employer on non-monetary employee perquisites is non-deductible u/s 35(a)(ii).
30% of any sum payable to a RESIDENT is disallowed u/s 35(b)(i) if TDS is not deducted or not paid before return due date u/s 263(1).
100% of interest, royalty, or fees payable to a NON-RESIDENT is disallowed u/s 35(b)(ii) for TDS failure.
If TDS is deducted/paid in a subsequent year, the disallowed 30% or 100% is allowed as a deduction in that payment year.

flow.title: TDS Default Disallowance Mechanism
steps: Identify payee (Resident vs Non-Resident)
Check if TDS deducted during tax year
Verify TDS remitted on/before return due date
Apply 30% disallowance for Resident default
Apply 100% disallowance for Non-Resident default

topics.example: A company pays ₹14L salary to a resident employee without TDS. 30% of ₹14L (₹4.20 lakhs) is disallowed in current year PGBP computation.
remember: Disallowance for TDS default to RESIDENTS is 30%; for NON-RESIDENTS it is 100%.
mistakes: Permanently disallowing TDS default expenses; they are allowable in the year TDS is subsequently remitted.

quiz.q: MNO Ltd. deducted TDS from resident professional fees but paid it after return due date u/s 263(1). Result?
o: 30% disallowed in current year and allowed in payment year
100% disallowed in current year and allowed in payment year
quiz.why: For resident TDS defaults, 30% is disallowed in the default year and allowed in the tax year TDS is deposited.

quiz.q: What percentage of royalty payable to a non-corporate non-resident is disallowed for failure to deduct TDS?
quiz.why: Section 35(b)(ii) mandates 100% disallowance for TDS defaults on payments to non-residents.

topics.title: Disallowances in Case of Partnership Firms and LLPs
explain: Remuneration paid to non-working partners is completely disallowed.
Remuneration or interest not authorized by or not in accordance with partnership deed is disallowed.
Interest paid to partners exceeding 12% simple interest per annum is disallowed.
Working partner remuneration is capped: On first ₹6 lakh book profit (or loss) -> ₹3,00,000 or 90% of book profit (whichever higher); On balance -> 60%.
Book profit means net profit adjusted by adding back partner remuneration deducted in P&L.

flow.title: Working Partner Remuneration Limit Test
steps: Calculate Book Profit before partner remuneration
Apply 90% (or ₹3L min) on first ₹6 lakh Book Profit
Apply 60% on balance Book Profit above ₹6 lakh
Sum up to find Maximum Allowable Remuneration
Disallow actual remuneration exceeding this limit

topics.example: A firm has ₹10 lakhs book profit. Max allowable partner remuneration: (90% of ₹6L = ₹5.4L) + (60% of ₹4L = ₹2.4L) = ₹7,80,000. Any excess paid is disallowed.
remember: Max allowable interest rate on partner capital/loan is 12% simple interest p.a.
mistakes: Calculating partner remuneration limits on book profits without adding back partner remuneration debited to P&L.

quiz.q: A partnership firm pays 15% interest p.a. on capital to partners as authorized by deed. Disallowance rate u/s 35(e) is:
quiz.why: Interest is allowed up to 12% p.a.; the excess 3% (15% - 12%) is disallowed.

quiz.q: A firm reports a book profit of ₹10,00,000. What is the maximum allowable working partner remuneration deduction?
quiz.why: First ₹6L @90% = ₹5.4L. Balance ₹4L @60% = ₹2.4L. Total allowable = ₹7.8L.

topics.title: Payments to Relatives & Cash Payment Disallowances
explain: Excessive or unreasonable payments made to relatives/specified persons can be disallowed by AO u/s 36(2).
Expenditure payments exceeding ₹10,000 made in a single day to a person in cash are 100% disallowed u/s 36(4).
For goods transport operators, the single-day cash payment limit is enhanced to ₹35,000 u/s 36(6).
Rule 26 provides exceptions where cash payments > ₹10,000 are allowed (e.g., payments to banks, RBI, govt legal tender, farmers for agricultural produce).
If an expense was allowed on accrual basis in year 1, and cash payment > ₹10,000 is made in year 2, it is taxed as deemed PGBP income in year 2 u/s 36(5).

flow.title: Cash Disallowance Test u/s 36(4)
steps: Check aggregate daily cash payment to a person
Identify payee type (Transport operator vs Others)
Check limit (₹35,000 for transport, ₹10,000 others)
Verify if covered under Rule 26 exceptions
Disallow 100% expenditure if limit exceeded

topics.example: Making 4 cash payments of ₹8,000 (total ₹32,000) in one day to a supplier exceeds ₹10,000, causing full ₹32,000 to be disallowed u/s 36(4).
remember: Transport operator daily cash limit is ₹35,000; general daily cash limit is ₹10,000.
mistakes: Paying via crossed cheque and expecting exemption; only specified account payee cheques or online banking modes avoid disallowance.

quiz.q: Mr. Raj paid salary of ₹12,00,000 to his brother. AO determined fair market value as ₹7,50,000. Amount disallowed u/s 36(2)?
quiz.why: Excessive amount over fair value is disallowed (₹12,00,000 - ₹7,50,000 = ₹4,50,000).

quiz.q: PQR Ltd. paid freight charges of ₹34,000 in cash to a transport operator in a single day. Disallowed sum u/s 36(4)?
quiz.why: For transport operators, cash payment up to ₹35,000 per day is allowed. ₹34,000 is within limit.

topics.title: Certain Deductions Allowed on Actual Payment Basis Only
explain: Specified expenses are deductible ONLY in the year actually paid, irrespective of accounting method followed.
Inclusions: Taxes, duties, cess, employer PF/ESI contributions, leave encashment, bonus/commission, bank interest, railway asset fees.
If paid after tax year end BUT on or before return filing due date u/s 263(1), deduction is allowed in that tax year.
Sum payable to Micro or Small Enterprises (MSME) beyond section 15 MSMED Act time limit (15/45 days) is deductible ONLY in actual payment year.
Conversion of unpaid bank interest into a loan/debenture is NOT treated as actual payment.

flow.title: Section 37 Payment Due Date Test
steps: Identify statutory tax/interest/MSME expense
Check actual payment date
If MSME, enforce strict 15/45 days limit
For others, check if paid before return due date u/s 263(1)
Allow in current year if paid in time; else allow in payment year

topics.example: GST liability incurred in March 2027 is remitted on April 15, 2027 (before return filing due date). It is allowed as deduction in T.Y. 2026-27.
remember: MSME payments made beyond 15 days (no agreement) or 45 days (written agreement) are allowed ONLY on actual payment basis.
mistakes: Assuming conversion of overdue bank interest into a new loan constitutes payment under section 37.

quiz.q: Hari converted unpaid bank interest of ₹15 lakhs into a funded term loan during the year. How much interest is deductible?
o: Allowed only when converted loan is actually repaid
quiz.why: Conversion of unpaid interest into a loan is not actual payment; deduction arises only upon actual loan repayment.

quiz.q: An assessee owes money to a Micro enterprise. Payment is made 90 days later (beyond 45 days agreement limit). Deduction is allowed:
o: On accrual basis in liability year
Only in the tax year of actual payment
quiz.why: Under section 37(2)(g), MSME payments made beyond MSMED Act limits are allowed strictly in the year of actual payment.

topics.title: Deemed Business Profits and Foreign Exchange Fluctuation
explain: Remission or cessation of a previously allowed trading liability is taxed as deemed business income u/s 38(1)(a).
Bad debt recovered subsequently is taxed as business profit in recovery year u/s 38(1)(d), even if business ceased.
Brought forward business losses of a defunct business can be set off against deemed profits u/s 38 even after 8 years.
Section 42 adjusts asset cost for foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations at the time of making payment.
Foreign exchange liability variations are added to or deducted from the actual cost of imported capital assets.

flow.title: Foreign Exchange Adjustment to Asset Cost
steps: Import business capital asset on credit
Repay foreign currency loan installment
Calculate exchange fluctuation difference in INR
Adjust (add/subtract) difference to actual asset cost
Recalculate future block depreciation on adjusted cost

topics.example: A company imports machinery from Germany. Due to exchange fluctuation during loan repayment, liability increases by ₹3,50,000. This ₹3.5L is added to actual cost of machinery.
remember: Deemed business profits u/s 38 are taxable even if the original business is no longer in existence.
mistakes: Treating foreign currency capital asset loan exchange variations as direct P&L revenue losses.

quiz.q: A company acquired machinery from Germany. On loan repayment, exchange fluctuation increased liability by ₹3,50,000. Treatment u/s 42?
o: Treated as revenue loss in P&L
Added to actual cost of machinery
quiz.why: Under section 42, foreign exchange variations on foreign currency asset borrowings are added/deducted from actual cost.

quiz.q: Unabsorbed loss of a defunct business can be set off against deemed business income u/s 38:
o: Even after the expiry of 8 years
Cannot be set off at all
quiz.why: Section 38(3) allows defunct business losses to be set off against section 38 deemed profits even beyond 8 years.

topics.title: Stamp Duty Value as Full Value of Consideration for Stock-in-Trade
explain: If land/building held as stock-in-trade is transferred below Stamp Duty Value (SDV), SDV is taken as full value of consideration.
Safe Harbour Rule: If SDV does not exceed 110% of actual consideration received, actual consideration is taken.
SDV on the date of agreement can be taken if part consideration was received via banking/online mode on/before agreement date.
If consideration was received in cash on agreement date, SDV on registration date must be used.
AO can refer valuation to a Valuation Officer if taxpayer claims SDV exceeds fair market value.

flow.title: Section 53 Full Value Determination
steps: Compare actual consideration with SDV
Check if SDV <= 110% of consideration
If yes, adopt Actual Consideration
If no, check agreement date non-cash advance
Adopt Agreement SDV (if advance non-cash) or Registration SDV

topics.example: A builder sells a flat (stock-in-trade) for ₹100 lakhs. SDV is ₹108 lakhs. Since ₹108L does not exceed 110% of ₹100L (₹110L), full value of consideration remains ₹100 lakhs.
remember: Safe harbour limit under section 53 is 110% of actual consideration.
mistakes: Using agreement date SDV when advance consideration was received in cash.

quiz.q: A builder sells land stock for ₹100 lakhs. Registration date SDV is ₹108 lakhs. Full value of consideration u/s 53 is:
quiz.why: Since SDV (₹108L) does not exceed 110% of actual consideration (₹110L), actual consideration ₹100L is taken.

quiz.q: To adopt SDV on agreement date instead of registration date, advance consideration must be received:
o: By account payee cheque/online mode on or before agreement date
By bearer cheque on registration date
quiz.why: Section 53(c) requires consideration/part thereof to be received by specified banking/online mode on or before agreement date.

topics.title: Maintenance of Books of Accounts and Penalties
explain: Specified professionals (legal, medical, engineering, CA, IT, architecture, film artist) must maintain books if gross receipts exceed ₹1,50,000 in all 3 preceding years.
Prescribed professional books: Cash book, journal, ledger, bills/receipts copies (>₹250), payment vouchers (<=₹250).
Non-specified business/profession: Individuals/HUFs maintain books if income > ₹2,50,000 or turnover > ₹25,00,000.
Others (Firms/Companies): Maintain books if income > ₹1,20,000 or turnover > ₹10,00,000 in any 1 of 3 preceding years.
Books must be retained for 7 tax years from the end of relevant tax year; penalty for failure is ₹25,000 u/s 441.

flow.title: Books Maintenance Obligation Test
steps: Check profession/business type
If specified profession, test ₹1,50,000 limit across all 3 years
If individual business, test ₹2.5L income / ₹25L turnover limit
Maintain prescribed Rule 46 books if limits crossed
Retain books for mandatory 7 tax years

topics.example: A newly set up consultancy firm estimates gross receipts of ₹28 lakhs. Being an individual business > ₹25L turnover, it must maintain books u/s 62.
remember: Books of accounts must be retained for 7 tax years from the end of the relevant tax year.
mistakes: Assuming specified professionals must cross ₹2,50,000 income; their limit is ₹1,50,000 gross receipts in all 3 preceding years.

quiz.q: Mr. Ravi sets up a consultancy business (non-specified) with estimated gross receipts of ₹28 lakhs. Obligation u/s 62?
o: Required to maintain books as receipts exceed ₹25 lakhs
Books required only if income exceeds ₹10 lakhs
quiz.why: For individuals carrying on business/profession, turnover exceeding ₹25,00,000 mandates maintaining books.

quiz.q: For how many tax years are books of accounts and documents required to be retained u/s 62?
quiz.why: Rule 46(8) specifies retaining books for a period of 7 tax years from the end of the relevant tax year.

topics.title: Compulsory Tax Audit Requirements and Limits
explain: Business turnover threshold for mandatory tax audit is > ₹1 Crore.
Enhanced Business Threshold: Limit is ₹10 Crores if aggregate cash receipts and cash payments are each <= 5% of total receipts/payments.
Profession gross receipts threshold for mandatory tax audit is > ₹50 Lakhs.
Tax audit report must be submitted by 'specified date' (30th September of the succeeding financial year).
Fee for failure to get accounts audited u/s 428(c): ₹75,000 for delay up to 1 month; ₹1,50,000 for delay beyond 1 month.

flow.title: Business Tax Audit Threshold Flow
steps: Determine total business turnover/receipts
Check cash receipts <= 5% and cash payments <= 5%
If cash <= 5%, apply ₹10 Crore threshold
If cash > 5%, apply ₹1 Crore threshold
Conduct tax audit before 30th September if exceeded

topics.example: A trader has ₹3.80 crore turnover with 3% cash receipts and 4% cash payments. Since cash transactions are under 5% and turnover is under ₹10 Crores, no tax audit is required.
remember: Specified date for tax audit is 30th September of the financial year succeeding the relevant tax year.
mistakes: Treating non-account payee cheques as non-cash transactions; law deems non-account payee cheques as CASH.

quiz.q: Trader A has ₹3.80 crore turnover. Cash receipts are 3% and cash payments 4%. Required to audit u/s 63?
o: No, turnover does not exceed ₹10 crore and cash transactions <= 5%
No, audit applies only to companies
quiz.why: When cash receipts and payments are each <= 5%, the tax audit turnover threshold increases from ₹1 crore to ₹10 crores.

quiz.q: What is the penalty fee u/s 428(c) for failure/delay beyond 1 month in furnishing tax audit report?
quiz.why: Section 428(c) imposes ₹75,000 fee for delay up to 1 month and ₹1,50,000 for delay beyond 1 month.

topics.title: Presumptive Taxation Schemes for Residents
explain: Section 58(2) normal business presumptive rate: 6% of digital/banking turnover and 8% of cash turnover (turnover limit <= ₹2 Cr, or ₹3 Cr if cash receipts <= 5%).
Presumptive scheme applies to resident Individuals, HUFs, and Partnership firms (excluding LLPs).
Goods Transport Operators u/s 58: Heavy vehicle (>12,000 kg gross weight) = ₹1,000/ton/month; Other vehicle = ₹7,50,000/vehicle/month (Max 10 vehicles owned).
Specified Professionals u/s 58: Deemed profit is 50% of gross receipts (limit <= ₹50 Lakhs, or ₹75 Lakhs if cash receipts <= 5%).
If an eligible assessee opts out of presumptive scheme in any of 5 subsequent years, they cannot re-enter presumptive scheme for 5 subsequent tax years.

flow.title: Presumptive Business Profit Rate Test u/s 58
steps: Check turnover limit (<= ₹2 Cr or ₹3 Cr if cash <= 5%)
Identify digital/banking receipts vs cash receipts
Apply 6% rate on banking/digital turnover
Apply 8% rate on cash turnover
Sum up to find Deemed PGBP Income

topics.example: A retailer has ₹1.80 Cr turnover (₹1.60 Cr via digital payments, ₹20L cash). Presumptive income: (6% of 1.60Cr = ₹9.6L) + (8% of 20L = ₹1.6L) = ₹11.20 lakhs.
remember: LLPs are NOT eligible for presumptive taxation under section 58.
mistakes: Applying goods carriage presumptive taxation when the assessee owns more than 10 goods vehicles at any time in the year.

quiz.q: Which of the following assessees is NOT eligible for presumptive taxation under section 58 for normal business?
quiz.why: Section 58 explicitly excludes LLPs from opting for presumptive taxation.

quiz.q: A resident professional (gross receipts ₹40 lakhs, cash 2%) opts for section 58 presumptive scheme. Deemed income?
quiz.why: For specified professionals, presumptive income is 50% of total gross receipts.

topics.title: Income Partly Agricultural and Partly Business
explain: Composite income from growing and manufacturing tea in India: 40% Business Income, 60% Agricultural Income.
Composite income from rubber products derived from rubber plants grown in India: 35% Business Income, 65% Agricultural Income.
Coffee grown and cured in India: 25% Business Income, 75% Agricultural Income.
Coffee grown, cured, roasted, and grounded in India: 40% Business Income, 60% Agricultural Income.
Income from saplings or seedlings grown in a nursery is 100% agricultural income regardless of basic land operations.

flow.title: Composite Income Apportionment Steps
steps: Compute total composite profits of plantation
Deduct allowable growing and processing costs
Identify composite product (Tea/Rubber/Coffee)
Apply specific prescribed percentage for Business
Treat balance percentage as exempt Agricultural Income

topics.example: A tea grower in Shimla earns ₹4,00,000 net profit from growing and manufacturing tea. Business income is 40% (₹1,60,000) and Agricultural income is 60% (₹2,40,000).
remember: Rubber = 35% Business; Tea = 40% Business; Coffee (grown & cured) = 25% Business.
mistakes: Apportioning coffee sales when operations (curing/roasting) are done OUTSIDE India; foreign operations make 100% of income taxable business income.

quiz.q: What percentage of composite income from growing and manufacturing tea in India is deemed to be taxable business income?
quiz.why: Rule 271 specifies that 40% of income from sale of tea grown and manufactured in India is business income.

quiz.q: Income derived from saplings and seedlings grown in a nursery in India is treated as:
quiz.why: Section 2(5)(d) deems all nursery sapling/seedling income as 100% agricultural income.
